why_how.text: A distraction diverts driving attention by taking the hands off the wheel, the eyes off the road or the mind away from driving.
Distracted driving can cause crashes that seriously injure drivers, passengers, pedestrians or other road users.
Avoid phone conversations, texting, arguments, emotional passenger conversations and eating while driving.
Before driving, make sure children and pets are properly secured.
The handbook's adult-device section generally prohibits using, holding or supporting a phone or other wireless communication device while driving, subject to its listed exceptions.
An officer who observes a violation of the adult-device restriction may stop the driver.
For drivers older than eighteen, the stated hands-free allowance requires no holding or supporting the device and no manual entry of letters, numbers or symbols.
The stated adult-device allowance permits activation or deactivation with only one touch or swipe.
The adult-device exceptions allow reporting an emergency to police, a hospital, a health provider, a fire department or a similar emergency organization.
The adult-device exceptions permit holding a phone to the ear during a call if starting or ending the call takes a single touch or swipe.
A listed exception allows adults stopped at a traffic signal, or parked along a road or highway, to handle a device during an emergency or road closure.
First responders may use electronic devices as part of their official work under a listed adult-device exception.
The listed adult-device exceptions cover utility workers operating utility vehicles in certain emergencies or outage situations.
A licensed operator's use of amateur radio is a listed adult-device exception.
